zh.title: 班加羅爾HAL機場啟用直升機RNP CAT H進場程序，將進場時間縮短至4分鐘
zh.summary: 印度班加羅爾HAL機場啟用直升機專用衛星導航程序；進場時間縮短至4分鐘。
body: 印度班加羅爾的HAL機場已正式啟用「H類所需導航性能」（RNP CAT H）直升機進場程序，成為印度首個啟用此類專用程序的機場。該系統採用精確的衛星導航技術，引導直升機沿著針對旋翼機飛行特性設計的三維飛行路徑降落，將直升機進場時間從原本的約12分鐘顯著縮短至4分鐘。
這項新進場程序由印度機場管理局（AAI）負責開發，並由印度航空工業公司（HAL）的測試飛行員完成試飛驗證，最終獲得印度民用航空總局（DGCA）的營運批准。此程序旨在於惡劣天氣條件下提升直升機的機場進出能力，同時讓旋翼機得以遵循更高效且可預測的航線運作。
大幅縮短進場時間能提升緊急醫療救護、搜救任務、災害應變及政府緊急航班的營運反應效率，並降低飛行員在關鍵階段的工作負擔。此外，更直接的進場路線亦能減少不必要的航程、降低燃油消耗，並減少航行於人口密集區域上空的時間，進而降低整體噪音影響。HAL董事局主席兼總經理拉維·K（Ravi K）表示，此項成果是印度航空生態系統的重要里程碑。
在班加羅爾HAL機場啟用該程序的大約一個月前，印度甫於安得拉邦的雲達瓦里直升機場（Undavalli Heliport）批准了該國首個直升機點對點（PinS）儀表進場程序。相較於主要用於缺乏傳統儀表設施之直升機場的PinS程序，HAL機場的RNP CAT H程序是印度首個在直升機與定翼機共用之機場環境中投入營運的系統。

en.title: Bengaluru HAL Airport Operationalises RNP CAT H Approach, Cutting Helicopter Arrival Times
en.summary: Bengaluru's HAL Airport operationalises RNP CAT H helicopter approach, reducing arrival times from 12 to four minutes.
body: HAL Airport in Bengaluru has operationalised a Required Navigation Performance Category H (RNP CAT H) approach procedure specifically designed for helicopters, becoming the first airport in India to deploy such a system. The precision satellite-guided flight path allows rotorcraft to follow three-dimensional arrival routes tailored to their flight characteristics, cutting approach times from around 12 minutes down to roughly four minutes.

The procedure was developed by the Airports Authority of India (AAI), validated through flight trials conducted by HAL test pilots, and granted operational approval by the Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA). Designed around rotorcraft performance capabilities—including the ability to slow rapidly, fly steeper approach profiles, and operate at lower speeds—the system enhances airport access during poor weather conditions while enabling safer navigation around terrain and urban obstacles.

The eight-minute reduction in approach times is intended to improve operational responsiveness and reduce pilot workload during critical missions, including emergency medical flights, search and rescue, disaster response, and urgent government operations. Direct satellite-based routing also reduces unnecessary track miles, cuts fuel consumption, and decreases time spent over densely populated areas, thereby lowering the overall noise footprint. Ravi K, Chairman and Managing Director of HAL, described the operationalisation as a significant milestone for India’s aviation ecosystem.

The operational milestone comes barely a month after India approved its first Point-in-Space (PinS) instrument approach procedure for helicopters at Undavalli Heliport in Andhra Pradesh. While PinS procedures are designed primarily for heliports without conventional instrument infrastructure, the new RNP CAT H procedure at HAL Airport represents the country's first system operationalised in an airport environment shared by helicopters and fixed-wing aircraft.
